newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New Philippine military chief installed.
newsitem.headline: New Philippine military chief installed.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Thursday installed an air force general known for being a disciplinarian as new Philippine armed forces chief, ordering him to keep soldiers in line so they would not lose the people's trust.
Lieutenant-General Arnulfo Acedera took over command of the country's 107,000-strong military from General Arturo Enrile, who has retired.
Ramos, referring to media reports about involvement of some military men in organised crime in recent years, including kidnapping for ransom, said there should be "moral renewal" in the armed forces.
"Every negative incident that involves a soldier betrays and diminishes (the people's) trust," he said.
Senior officers described Acedera as a disciplinarian and a man who would have no qualms about tangling with politicians meddling in army affairs.

The military was widely unpopular during the martial law rule of late president Ferdinand Marcos because of its abuses. It regained its prestige when several officers, including Ramos, rose up against Marcos and ousted him in a popular revolt in 1986.
Its image plummeted again in the late 1980s when it tried to unseat then president Corazon Aquino in six failed coup attempts.
Ramos concluded a peace deal with the army rebels after he won the 1992 presidential elections and the military has remained loyal to the government since then.
